sections.Interpretation: Haemoglobin of 20.4 g/dL and haematocrit of 61% indicate marked erythrocytosis. The red-cell indices are reduced, consistent with a microcytic and hypochromic red-cell population. Mild leucocytosis with neutrophil predominance and thrombocytosis, together with headache, plethoric facies and pruritus after bathing, raise suspicion of a myeloproliferative neoplasm such as polycythaemia vera, although secondary causes of erythrocytosis must be excluded. Further assessment should include JAK2 V617F testing, serum erythropoietin level and arterial oxygen saturation.
sections.Comment/recommendation: CRITICAL VALUE: Haematocrit 61%. This result is flagged as critical. Urgent haematology referral is recommended. JAK2 testing should be performed, and venesection should be considered to reduce haematocrit and lower thrombotic risk, with clinical review as indicated.
